text:
alex: Heads up — the policy decision surface exploded on the canary and we're seeing 95/99p tail latency spikes. Noticed this after adding the new regional-preference composer.
maria: Ugh. Saw that in the dashboard. Query latency went from ~45ms median to 180ms p95 for that tenant slice. :grimacing:
jonathan: Do we have an attribution trace? Is it evaluation cost (policy eval CPU) or runtime decision fanout (more adapters called)?
sarah: From traces it looks like the policy graph eval count doubled and we ended up calling 3 adapters where previously 1 was enough. So both CPU and downstream fanout.
alex: My read: combinatorial rules + late binds caused the runtime to expand matchers. We need a pruning strategy (compile-time + runtime guardrails) and an actionable rollback playbook.
eva: Agree. Proposed options:
  1) Compile-time static pruning: run a saturation pass that removes dominated branches (safe but conservative).
  2) Runtime short-circuit heuristics: stop eval after an accept threshold (faster but might hide correctness issues).
  3) Adapter-level de-dup / memoization: prevent redundant downstream calls during a single decision.
maria: Also think we should add an explainability token to the decision so we can know which branch caused the fanout in prod logs (low overhead tag).
jonathan: For short-term rollback we should be able to flip a single flag that restores the previous compiled policy bundle. Do we have a feature toggle path for policy bundles?
sarah: We do — control-plane stores compiled bundles with version ids. We can pin tenants to bundle vX. Rolling back is `curl -X POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/pin -d '{"bundle":"vX-2026-03-18"}'` from the admin plane. Ops should have runbook.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout paused at 7% due to p95 > 150ms for tenant=acme. See: https://console/redwood/rollouts/123
eva: Good catch. For a proper playbook I suggest:
  - Immediate mitigation: pin affected tenants to last-good bundle (fastest)
  - Short-term patch: enable runtime short-circuit with a strict budget (to buy time)
  - Medium-term: run compile-time pruning + add dominance checks to the composer
  - Long-term: add policy simulation test in CI that runs sampled real traffic against new bundles
maria: We need concrete rollback criteria/alerts. My proposal:
  - Canary p95 increase > 50ms vs baseline OR
  - Error rate increase > 1% absolute OR
  - Downstream adapter call count per request > 2x baseline
jonathan: Those are sensible. For the runtime short-circuit budget we should be explicit: max_evals_per_request=5 and max_adapter_calls=2 as defaults until we validate.
sarah: Will create a quick toggle: `policy.runtime.guard.max_evals=5` and `policy.runtime.guard.max_adapter_calls=2`. Toggle lives in config service and is hot-updatable.
eva: For compile-time pruning algorithm sketch:
  - Compute dominance: node A dominates node B if A's predicates imply B's predicates and A has equal-or-better route cost.
  - Remove dominated nodes unless marked as explicitly preserved by policy author.
  - Run a shallow equivalence check to ensure decision semantics are preserved for existing unit prompt set (CI tests)
alex: That dominance check is cool. But careful: cost metrics are dynamic (latency/capacity). We should only use static metadata (region/tier/tenant constraints) for pruning; runtime cost should drive runtime routing, not compile pruning.
maria: Right — compile prune only on logical implication. Runtime decisions can still re-rank by cost.
jonathan: Telemetry tweaks we need right away:
  - emit `policy.eval_count` per request
  - emit `policy.adapter_calls` per request
  - emit `policy.pruned_branches` when compile-prune makes removals
  - correlate these with latency spans in traces
sarah: I'll add those metrics + a Grafana dashboard. Initial alert thresholds per maria's criteria.
eva: Also add a small sampling `policy.explain_sample_rate=0.01` that ships full decision trace for 1% of requests to trace problematic cases without overload.
alex: Can we make rollback scripted? Example command for ops:
```
# pin tenant to previous good bundle
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme/pin \
  -d '{"bundle":"bundle-20260315-abc123"}'
```
ops-bot: ops-checklist: ensure admin token used from ephemeral vault credentials and confirm the tenant is pinned by querying `/api/v1/tenants/acme`.
maria: Post-rollback verification steps:
  - confirm p95 back to baseline within 10 minutes
  - ensure no increase in 5xx downstream errors
  - run a golden prompt set against the rolled-back bundle to verify semantics
jonathan: One more risk: pruning may hide a correctness bug if policy author relied on side-effects in downstream adapters. We must educate authors: adapters should be pure responders (no side-effect causality used in policy).
eva: I'll write a short doc for policy authors and add a lint rule: policy specs that reference adapter-side-effects will fail compilation unless explicitly flagged.
alex: Ok action items assigned:
  - sarah: add metrics + dashboard + toggle endpoints (ETA today)
  - eva: compile-time dominance PR and author docs (ETA EOW)
  - maria: alert thresholds + explain sampling config (ETA tomorrow)
  - jonathan: add CI simulation harness that runs sampled traces against candidate bundles (ETA 2 weeks)
  - ops: practice scripted rollback in staging and confirm runbook (ETA tomorrow)
alex: Thanks everyone. If anything else crops up, post here and we can escalate to a hotfix branch. :thumbsup:
